messages:
maria_cs: Quick heads-up — Starling onboarding hit a burst of 429s during SDK warmup this morning, plus a couple of intermittent 401s. Call in 10 to triage. Logs pasted below.
max_eng: thanks. can you paste the exact user-agent + sample request? are they using our browser SDK or server SDK?
lia_onboard: they reported using node SDK from a lambda pool, ~150 concurrent cold inits. preflight requests spiked.
maria_cs: sample curl from their engineer:
```
curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx\" -H \"User-Agent: starling-service/1.2.0\" -d '{\"input\":\"hi\"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
maria_cs: logs show repeated 429s with body: `{\"error\":\"rate_limited\",\"retry_after\":0.5}` and occasional 401 `invalid_token` when their refresh lambda overlaps.
max_eng: two quick suspects: (1) preflight/handshake fanout from cold starts, (2) ephemeral token refresh collision.
max_eng: mitigation suggestions: stagger token refresh (random jitter), use a short-LRU token cache in the pool, and add preflight coalescing on their side.
lia_onboard: i've told them to set a 300ms splay on startup and to reduce parallel preflight to 10 per instance. also asked to switch to persistent http2 connections if lambda runtime allows.
onboard-bot: deploy-check: observed 150 requests/s from starling-org during 08:03-08:06 UTC, peak concurrency ~165, 429 rate 18%.
maria_cs: noted renewal risk = medium if we can't stabilize by EOD next Tue. Need eng assist and a quick config doc to hand them.
max_eng: can we ship a short playbook? i can draft lines:
- detect 429 -> exponential backoff with cap at 2s
- preflight coalesce: single preflight per container with shared promise
- token refresh: leader election per pool / or add 100ms jitter
- if persistent 429s: throttle client-side or request dedicated capacity trial
lia_onboard: adding checklist to the thread so CSM can send:
1) Add jitter to refresh and coarse-leader for token renewals
2) Reduce parallel preflight to <=10 per container / use warm startup hooks
3) Enable keepalive / http2 pooling on SDK call layer
4) If 429 persists after client fixes -> open a Dedicated trial request (CS to qualify)
maria_cs: perfect. max, can you paste the snippet for token-leader pattern?
max_eng: quick Node example:
```
// simple leader-refresh with shared promise
let refreshPromise = null;
async function getToken() {
  if (refreshPromise) return refreshPromise;
  refreshPromise = refreshToken();
  try { return await refreshPromise; } finally { refreshPromise = null; }
}
```
max_eng: also told them to surface telemetry headers: X-Request-Id, X-CSM-Org so we can correlate spikes.
lia_onboard: i'll follow up on the call and log action items. maria, i'll include renewal note and timelines in the handoff doc. :calendar: 
maria_cs: thanks — ping me after call, i'll update the health rubric and flag for sales if we need committed capacity offer. :thumbsup:
max_eng: misc: if they can reproduce locally, ask them to run a short load with `concurrency=50` and `stagger=100ms` and send us the traces. that helps rule out network spikes.
lia_onboard: call started. moving to quick triage channel. will paste summary here after.
